chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from a man from Khuzaa, from Aslami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Learn Arabic, for it is the speech of God with which He spoke to His creation, and clean the chewing teeth, and wear the rings on the fingertips. Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hussein, the compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: This hadith has also been narrated by Abu Saeed al-Adami, who said at its end: 'Wear the rings,' meaning place the rings on the ends of the fingers and do not place them on the tips of the thumb, for it is narrated that this was the practice of the people of Lot.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of learning Arabic and the proper way to wear rings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the linguistic sanctity of Arabic as the medium of divine creation, linking it to physical purity (tidiness of teeth) and specific social etiquette (ring placement). The scholarly note clarifies that wearing rings on the very tip of the finger, rather than the distal phalanx, is a distinctive practice attributed to the people of Lot, serving as a marker of identity or imitation in early Islamic tradition.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-134 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, on the authority of a man from Khoza’at, on the authority of Aslami, on the authority of his father that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “You should learn Arabic since it is the language with which God has spoken to His servants. Utter the words properly.”

The compiler of the book - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hussein - may God be pleased with him - said, “This narration has also been narrated by Abu Saeed Adami who has added the following at the end, ‘and wear your rings on your little finger or your ring finger not on the thumb since that has been a practice of the people of Lot. ’”
